meta.document: Palm Beach County FL FY2026 Adopted Budget
meta.title: Palm Beach County — the money trail
meta.note: Palm Beach County, Florida — the state’s largest county by area, ~1.5 million people. This is the adopted all-funds budget for FY2026, $9.6 billion, grouped by function as the county reports it. Two honest caveats the county’s own documents make: about 21% ($2.0B) is Reserves held rather than spent, and about $968M is interfund transfers — the same dollars moving between funds — so the operating appropriation is roughly $4.58 billion. The Sheriff’s Office alone is $1.10B. The countywide operating millage is 4.5000 per $1,000 of value, on a $343B tax base. Every figure ties to the county’s FY2026 Budget in Brief and Fact Sheet, which agree to the dollar.

nodes.name: Public Safety
nodes.note: The Sheriff’s Office ($1.10B, the single largest agency), Fire Rescue, and county public-safety programs.

nodes.name: Reserves
nodes.note: Money budgeted but held in reserve, not spent unless the Commission appropriates it — about 21% of the whole budget.

nodes.name: Transportation
nodes.note: Roads, engineering, Palm Tran transit, and the county airports.

nodes.name: General Government
nodes.note: Countywide administration, the constitutional officers, elections, and property appraisal.

nodes.name: Interfund transfers
nodes.note: Money moved between county funds — counted in the headline total, so part of the $9.6B is the same dollars moving once.

nodes.name: Physical Environment
nodes.note: Water Utilities, environmental resources, and physical infrastructure.

nodes.name: Internal Services
nodes.note: Fleet, risk management, and shared internal services.

nodes.name: Human Services
nodes.note: Community services, youth services, and health programs.

nodes.name: Non-Departmental
nodes.note: Countywide costs not tied to one department.
